findings.reason: without an ordering between §44 and §45 the queue admits two workers holding an exclusive claim on the same module, which is the collision the depends-on declarations exist to prevent.
findings.text: §44 and §45 are both `implementable` and both declare `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` in their write paths, but `plan-section-depends-on` gives each of them only `s43`, so neither waits on the other and a wave can dispatch both against one file; the earlier finding that both should wait on §43 was answered in a way that serialises them behind §43 but not against each other

findings.reason: as written the third case's stated control cannot be applied to the code the deliverable asks for, so the case is left with no falsifying control and the plan should restate the control against the shared predicate or state that two call sites remain.
findings.text: §44's third done-when case requires an unmeasured change to be "owed by both readings, not by one" and its third control is "treating an unmeasured change as covered in one reader alone", but the deliverable makes the write response and admission compute coverage "through one call with the same inputs", after which there is only one treatment of an unmeasured change and no second reader to mutate

response_events.note: plan-section-depends-on gains s45 waiting on s44, so the two plan_review.py sections run in order

wiring-1.note: plan-section-depends-on gains s45 waiting on s44, so the two plan_review.py sections run in order

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §46's anchors resolve at the base revision (`reckon/crew/obligations.py:2591`, `reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:123`, `reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:1460`), and §44's `reckon/mcp_deadlines.py:740` is exact; the `reckon/crew/routing.py` line offset in §44 is the same offset an earlier review declined.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §44's third done-when case and its third negative control describe two distinguishable coverage readers, while §44's deliverable replaces both with one call, so the control has no reader left to mutate.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §44 keeps the reproduction record in the run directory, and §46 runs its arms under the run directory the dispatch fence supplies; neither names a session scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the two sections introduce `tests/test_an_edit_owing_no_review_holds_no_queued_run.py` and `tests/test_a_request_waiting_on_a_queued_plan_review_is_a_wait.py`, which name the mechanism rather than a plan label, and no ticket or phase identifier reaches a symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §44's evidence supports only two candidate inputs (the plan file each caller reads, and the review records each sees) and its deliverable is to identify which, with both entry points named; §46 names both sites that build the duty, and its second producer was verified: `reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py` is registered as the stop hook in `~/.claude/settings.json`, and `reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:1461` rebuilds `QUEUED_AWAITING_SESSION_DUTY_KIND` from `row.get("session_refusal")` independently of the derivation at `reckon/crew/obligations.py:2589`.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §44 carries one deliverable (one coverage reading shared by the write response and admission) and §46 carries one (a request waiting on a queued plan review is a wait), each with its own controls.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §44 and §45 both declare `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` in their write paths and both declare only `s43` as a dependency, so once §43 lands the queue can dispatch them concurrently against one file.
